subject: English
intended_use: Practice question bank for Nepal Grade 11 & 12 English

schema_notes.correct_options: Array of option keys; supports single- and multi-select answers
schema_notes.is_multi_select: True when more than one option is correct

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the grammatically correct sentence adhering to subject-verb agreement:

options.text: Neither the teacher nor the students was present in the seminar.
Neither the teacher nor the students were present in the seminar.
Neither the teacher nor the students is present in the seminar.
Neither the teacher nor the students has attended.

questions.explanation: When two subjects are joined by "neither... nor", the verb agrees in number and person with the nearer subject ("students", plural), hence "were present".
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Transform into indirect speech: She said, "If I were you, I would consult a physician."

options.text: She advised me to consult a physician.
She told me that if she had been me she will consult a physician.
She said that if she was me she would have consulted.
She asked whether I consult a physician.

questions.explanation: The structure "If I were you, I would..." functions pragmatically as advice; reporting it directly with the reporting verb "advised + object + to-infinitive" is standard NEB English usage.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the grammatically complete conditional: "Had the pilot received timely meteorological radar warnings, the emergency landing ______."
questions.explanation: Inverted third conditional ("Had + Subject + V3") corresponds to "If + had + V3", which requires "would have + past participle" in the result clause.
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In Edgar Allan Poe's short story "The Oval Portrait" prescribed in NEB Class 11, what fatal obsession consumes the painter?

options.text: Stealing life and vitality from his young bride into the canvas
Escaping from a haunted Gothic castle
Finding alchemical gold in pigment mixtures

questions.explanation: In "The Oval Portrait", the painter is so monomaniacally consumed by transferring the lifelikeness of his bride onto the canvas that the portrait absorbs her vitality, causing her to perish at the final brushstroke.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Select the appropriate preposition: "The dispute was settled amicably ______ accordance with the national environmental guidelines."
questions.explanation: The fixed prepositional phrase in English idiom is "in accordance with".
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct verb form: "The principal had the electrician ______ the broken wiring in the laboratory before practical exams began."
questions.explanation: The causative structure "have + person (agent) + base form of verb (bare infinitive)" requires "repair". ("Have someone do something").
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Complete the sentence with correct inverted word order: "Seldom ______ such overwhelming unanimity in parliament."
questions.explanation: Negative and restrictive adverbs (seldom, rarely, hardly, scarcely, never) placed at the beginning of a clause trigger subject-auxiliary inversion: "Seldom have we witnessed...".
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In Kate Chopin's story "A Respectable Woman" (NEB Class 12), what complex inner struggle does Mrs. Baroda experience toward Gouverneur?

options.text: An unexpected, unsettling physical and emotional attraction that conflicts with social propriety
Anger regarding an old family feud

questions.explanation: Mrs. Baroda struggles between her conventional societal identity as a "respectable woman" and an irresistible sensual and emotional fascination with her husband's calm friend Gouverneur.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Convert into Passive Voice: "They believe that the archaeological site dates back to the Lichchhavi era."

options.text: The archaeological site was believed to date back to the Lichchhavi era.
It is believed that the archaeological site dates back to the Lichchhavi era.
The Lichchhavi era is believed to be dated back.

questions.explanation: Impersonal passive with reporting verbs: "They believe that..." transforms to "It is believed that..." preserving present tense.
questions.curriculum_note: NEB Model; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What is the closest antonym of the word "EPHEMERAL" as frequently encountered in literary texts?
questions.explanation: "Ephemeral" signifies lasting for a very short time. Its direct antonym is "Perpetual" or "Eternal" (lasting indefinitely).
questions.curriculum_note: Entrance Standard; Official Nepal NEB CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'I look forward to ___ you.'
questions.explanation: 'Look forward to' is followed by a gerund.
questions.curriculum_note: Official Nepal NEB Grade 12 CDC Curriculum aligned.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the synonym of 'begin'.
questions.explanation: 'Commence' means to begin.

She asked me where I was going.

questions.question: Choose the correct form: 'By the time we reached, the film ___.'

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Shakespeare's 'Macbeth' is a:

questions.question: What does 'magnanimous' mean?

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Identify the error in: 'He is more taller than his brother.'

questions.question: In 'Swimming is good exercise', the word 'Swimming' is a:

questions.subject: English
questions.question: What does 'procrastinate' mean?

questions.subject: English

Each of the boys has a bat.

questions.subject: English

A bridge was built by them.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.

options.text: She go to school every day.
She goes to school every day.
She going to school every day.
She gone to school every day.

questions.explanation: The past perfect 'had finished' shows an action completed before another past action.

questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and kindly.

questions.question: What is the passive form of 'He wrote a letter'?

options.text: A letter was written by him.
A letter is written by him.
A letter has been written by him.

Neither of the boys is ready.

questions.question: Identify the sentence containing a nominal (noun) clause:

options.text: What you have accomplished in the laboratory is genuinely remarkable.
The laboratory that stands on the hill is newly built.
We left the hall when the lecture ended.
She spoke softly because the baby was sleeping.

questions.explanation: "What you have accomplished in the laboratory" functions as the subject of the sentence, operating as a noun clause.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Fill in the blank: "The committee agreed _______ the recommendations submitted by the panel."
questions.explanation: One "agrees to" a proposal or recommendation, whereas one "agrees with" a person or opinion.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Choose the correct sentence regarding comma usage with non-restrictive relative clauses:

options.text: Dr. Sharma, who discovered the fossil, delivered the keynote lecture.
Dr. Sharma who discovered the fossil delivered the keynote lecture.
Dr. Sharma, who discovered the fossil delivered the keynote lecture.
Dr. Sharma who discovered the fossil, delivered the lecture.

questions.explanation: Non-defining (non-restrictive) relative clauses provide parenthetical extra information and must be bracketed by commas on both sides.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: Coherence in academic prose is achieved predominantly through:

options.text: Logical sequencing of ideas, transitional connectors, and consistent pronouns
Using the longest possible Latinized words exclusively
Writing paragraphs consisting of single words

questions.explanation: Coherence ensures smooth logical transitions and conceptual flow between sentences and paragraphs.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In formal technical report writing, the terms of reference section states:

options.text: The mandate, purpose, scope, and operational boundaries of the inquiry
The personal hobbies of the investigating officers
The dictionary bibliography of unrelated concepts

questions.explanation: Terms of reference delineate the authorized scope, objectives, and parameters guiding an investigative report.

questions.question: In formal email etiquette, a subject line should ideally be:

options.text: Concise, specific, and accurately descriptive of the email's content
A very long continuous paragraph of 50 words

questions.explanation: Effective email subject lines inform the recipient immediately and precisely of the message's topic and urgency.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: When preparing an academic summary, a student must strictly avoid:

options.text: Inserting personal unsupported opinions or extraneous external commentary
Retaining the central thesis of the original author
Using objective and concise academic vocabulary
Condensing lengthy paragraphs into essential assertions

questions.explanation: Summaries must remain objective representations of source material without adding uncorroborated editorial opinions.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A journalistic news lead sentence answering the core journalistic questions is called the:
questions.explanation: The summary lead immediately answers Who, What, Where, When, Why, and How in concise, punchy prose.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In creative writing, "showing rather than telling" means:

options.text: Dramatizing action, dialogue, and sensory experience instead of summarizing dry facts
Only providing bulleted checklists of traits

questions.explanation: "Show, don't tell" immerses readers in vivid scenes and observable behaviors rather than plain exposition.

questions.subject: English
questions.question: In poetry, the intentional repetition of initial consonant sounds across successive words is:

questions.subject: English
questions.question: A rhetorical device balancing opposing ideas in parallel grammatical constructions is:
